sites.name: Venera 3
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate impact location published for Venera 3 (20 N, 80 W); no data returned from the surface.
sites.summary: Venera 3 was the first spacecraft to reach another planet's surface — it crashed at 20 N, 80 W in 1966 and never answered.
narrative: Venera 3 launched in November 1965 to land on Venus. On 1 March 1966 it became the first spacecraft to reach the surface of another planet, impacting at about 20 degrees north, 80 degrees west, but its communications failed and no data was returned.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Venera 4
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate impact location published for Venera 4 (19 N, 38 W).
sites.summary: Venera 4 measured Venus' atmosphere during descent in 1967, then crushed at 19 N, 38 W.
narrative: Venera 4 launched in June 1967 and measured the Venusian atmosphere during descent, finding it hotter and denser than expected. On 18 October 1967 the lander impacted at about 19 degrees north, 38 degrees west.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Venera 5
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate impact location published for Venera 5 (1.5 S, 19 W).
sites.summary: Venera 5 descended into Venus' atmosphere in 1969 and was crushed at 1.5 S, 19 W.
narrative: Venera 5 launched in January 1969 to measure the Venusian atmosphere. On 16 May 1969 it descended to about 1.5 degrees south, 19 degrees west, where the pressure crushed the lander.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Venera 6
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude

sites.summary: Venera 6 measured Venus' atmosphere in 1969 before being crushed at 5 S, 23 W.
narrative: Venera 6 launched in November 1968 and measured the Venusian atmosphere during descent. On 17 January 1969 it was crushed at about 5 degrees south, 23 degrees west.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Venera 7
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate impact location published for Venera 7 (5 S, 351 E); converted to -9 longitude.
sites.summary: Venera 7 tipped over on landing in 1970 and transmitted weakly from 5 S, 9 W before falling silent.
narrative: Venera 7 launched in August 1970 to land on Venus. On 15 December 1970 it impacted at about 5 degrees south, 9 degrees west (351 degrees east), tipped over, and transmitted only a weak signal for 23 minutes.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Venera 8
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate impact location published for Venera 8 (10 S, 335 E); converted to -25 longitude.
sites.summary: Venera 8 measured Venus' surface conditions in 1972 before being crushed at 10 S, 25 W.
narrative: Venera 8 launched in July 1972 to measure surface conditions on Venus. On 22 July 1972 it impacted at about 10 degrees south, 25 degrees west (335 degrees east) and transmitted for about 50 minutes before being crushed.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Venera 9 lander
sites.categoryDetail: Robotic lander — first images from Venus surface
sites.status: Mission complete — lander remains on surface
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Landing within 150 km radius of 31.01 N, 291.64 E as published; converted to -68.36 longitude. Exact landfall unknown.
sites.summary: Venera 9 sent the first pictures from Venus' surface in 1975, then fell silent at 31.01 N, 68.36 W.
narrative: Venera 9 landed on 22 October 1975 within 150 km of 31.01 degrees north, 68.36 degrees west (291.64 degrees east) and returned the first images from the surface of Venus, showing a rocky plain under a bright sky. It transmitted for 53 minutes.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus. The exact landfall is known only to within 150 km, so the marker is shown as approximate.

sites.name: Venera 10 lander
sites.status: Mission complete — lander remains on surface
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Landing within 150 km radius of 15.42 N, 291.51 E as published; converted to -68.49 longitude.
sites.summary: Venera 10 landed three days after Venera 9 in 1975 and transmitted from 15.42 N, 68.49 W for 65 minutes.
narrative: Venera 10 landed on 25 October 1975 within 150 km of 15.42 degrees north, 68.49 degrees west (291.51 degrees east), about 2,200 km from Venera 9. It transmitted images and environmental data for 65 minutes.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.summary: Venera 11 landed on Christmas Day 1978 at 14 S, 61 W and measured the surface for 95 minutes.
narrative: Venera 11 landed on 25 December 1978 at about 14 degrees south, 61 degrees west (299 degrees east). It measured surface conditions for 95 minutes before falling silent.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.coordNote: Approximate landing location published for Venera 12 (7 S, 294 E); converted to -66 longitude.
sites.summary: Venera 12 landed the same day as Venera 11 in 1978, at 7 S, 66 W, and transmitted for 110 minutes.
narrative: Venera 12 landed on 25 December 1978 at about 7 degrees south, 66 degrees west (294 degrees east), the same day as Venera 11. It transmitted for 110 minutes.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Venera 13 lander
sites.categoryDetail: Robotic lander — first colour images from Venus surface
sites.status: Mission complete — lander remains on surface
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate landing location published for Venera 13 (7.5 S, 304.5 E); converted to -55.5 longitude.
sites.summary: Venera 13 sent the first colour pictures from Venus in 1982, surviving 127 minutes at 7.5 S, 55.5 W.
narrative: Venera 13 landed on 1 March 1982 at about 7.5 degrees south, 55.5 degrees west (304.5 degrees east), east of Phoebe Regio. It returned the first colour images from the Venus surface and survived for 127 minutes, far longer than its 32-minute design life.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.summary: Venera 14 landed 950 km from Venera 13 in 1982 and transmitted from 13.25 S, 49.9 W for 57 minutes.
narrative: Venera 14 landed on 5 March 1982 at about 13.25 degrees south, 49.9 degrees west (310.1 degrees east), about 950 km from Venera 13. It transmitted for 57 minutes.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Vega 1 lander
sites.status: Mission complete — lander remains on surface
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate landing location published for Vega 1 (7.5 N, 177.7 E).
sites.summary: Vega 1 landed on Venus in 1985 at 7.5 N, 177.7 E, then flew on to Halley's Comet — its lander is still there.
narrative: Vega 1 launched in December 1984 to land on Venus and then fly on to Halley's Comet. On 11 June 1985 its lander touched down at about 7.5 degrees north, 177.7 degrees east in Rusalka Planitia and transmitted for about 56 minutes.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

narrative: Vega 2 launched in December 1984 to land on Venus and then fly on to Halley's Comet. On 15 June 1985 its lander touched down at about 8.5 degrees south, 164.5 degrees east and transmitted for about 46 minutes.
The lander remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.

sites.name: Kosmos 482 descent craft
sites.status: Mission failed — descent craft impacted Venus
sites.coordSystem: IAU planetocentric Venus coordinates, east longitude
sites.coordNote: Approximate impact location published for Kosmos 482 (1.3 S, 305 E); converted to -55 longitude. The mission failed in Earth orbit and the descent craft fell to Venus.
sites.summary: Kosmos 482 was a Venera lander that failed in Earth orbit in 1972, then fell to Venus and crashed at 1.3 S, 55 W.
narrative: Kosmos 482 launched in March 1972 as a Venera lander, but its upper stage failed in Earth orbit. The descent craft remained in Earth orbit for 10 years, then fell to Venus and impacted on 3 May 1972 at about 1.3 degrees south, 55 degrees west (305 degrees east).
The descent craft remains where it struck, catalogued among the artificial objects on Venus.
